summary: Make fractal the physical runtime executable and the complete Nix product instead of an opt-in wrapper; prepare the coordinated installer and Home Manager consumer cutover.

replay.detail: No claim replay, projection rebuild, state-directory move or data migration. Immutable historical releases and signed payloads are not rewritten.

schema.detail: No database, wire or durable install-manifest schema change.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules, digest domains and PTY runtime payload and pins are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Cargo emits fractal. Current archives, native setup, macOS bundles and Home Manager-owned stable paths install physical fractal; packages.fractal selects the full product with web assets, PTY and canonical completions. Home Manager refuses foreign canonical files, directories and symlinks, including matching payload bytes, before changing the install layout; historical fractal-to-st3 links and physical executables with both exact reverse aliases remain eligible for atomic upgrades. The download installer decodes retained archives by their physical payload and launches their installed st3 command rather than a canonical forward alias the historical installer may not install. Setup preserves a default canonical command symlink to its running image even when the account's login PATH omits it; named instances still install their own copies. Temporary st/st3 reverse executable aliases and transitional package attributes remain explicit unfinished migration work, not completion evidence. The programs.smalltalk.fractalBinary.enable option is removed, including its former false setting; consumer configurations must remove that option atomically with the package pin and policy adoption. Existing service labels, bundle identifiers, state paths and historical release payloads remain unchanged.

downtime.detail: This source candidate performs no host deployment or restart. Installers retain atomic executable replacement and transaction rollback; managed service and seat adoption remains an owner-controlled readiness gate.

manual.detail: Do not adopt this candidate until the owning dotfiles configuration removes the obsolete option and approves the matching pin and policy together. Installer, package-layout, completion and native ownership proofs are pending; macOS must additionally pass native ABI, executing-image replacement/unlink, signing and rollback proof in its admitted lane. No build, test or operational receipt is claimed by this fragment. External consumers must select fractal before the temporary reverse aliases can be removed.

recovery.detail: A previous package pin requires its matching previous consumer configuration; do not mix the removed-option configuration contract across pins. Installer rollback preserves previous executable inodes, command links and signed app contents. Canonical uninstall requires positive running-image ownership and conservatively retains an unverified replacement rather than executing or deleting it. No persisted data rollback is required.
